purpose: Source-bound survey for relating the user's 2026-09-27 CHU clarification to HSWM without copying external sibling-repository material or reviving retired governance mechanisms.

included: local HSWM documents that mention the historical CHU boundary
non-secret metadata and short paraphrases from the sibling SYMPOSIUM CHU corpus
read-only ontology records returned by the configured ontology service
excluded: private logs, credentials, and source bytes from the sibling repository
claims that a finite graph store already implements the abstract CHU
performance or physical-world claims not established by a cited source

currentUserClarification.paraphrase: CHU is the broader abstract Computable Hyper Universe: it can contain real world models and HSWM. HSWM is the LLM-specific system within that broader concept. The user also proposes executable semantic-weight hypergraph memory, graph-native code and documents, and parallel LLM operation as a target software architecture.
currentUserClarification.interpretationBoundary: This survey records the clarification for the new dated research synthesis. It does not overwrite older user records or turn the proposed architecture into a measured result.

sources.finding: Defines CHU minimally as an abstract type universe with CHUPiece predicates; characterizes CHU as a stage/substrate on or over which other constructs operate. Its organizational mythology, workflow commands, and external-grounding assertions are not adopted by this survey.
sources.use: Supports separating abstract CHU from any finite memory, database, or HSWM instance.

sources.finding: States that the project CHU substrate and Pratt Chu spaces are different objects: the first is an abstract computation/predicate substrate and the second a categorical semantic model.

synthesisConstraints: CHU is an abstract umbrella/domain; a finite graph, database, world model, executable memory, Internet snapshot, or HSWM is an instance, region, or projection rather than CHU in full.
HSWM is an LLM-native cognitive system situated within CHU. It may implement a world-model role, but it does not exhaust real-world models or define the whole CHU.
Semantic Weight can be described as executable program/state only when its revision and execution semantics are specified; storage alone is not execution.

Documents, code, network resources, tensors, and graph views may be related through explicit mappings. A claim that all have already become one hypergraph is a target hypothesis, not current repository fact.
Use RDF, SHACL, SPARQL, JSON-LD, and PROV-O as interoperability views/contracts where applicable; they are not evidence that the abstract CHU has been realized.
